title: Termwise interval integration of normally summable continuous functions
statement:
Work over $\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $J$ be a countable set, let $a,b\in\mathbf R$ with $a\leq b$, and let $f_j:\mathbf R\to\mathbf C$ be continuous for each $j\in J$. Put $N_j=\sup_{a\leq x\leq b}|f_j(x)|$. If $\sum_{j\in J}N_j$ is summable, then
$$\sum_{j\in J}\int_a^b f_j(x)\,dx=\int_a^b\sum_{j\in J}f_j(x)\,dx,$$
where the series of integrals converges as the net of finite subsums and integration is ordinary interval integration. Also, for a continuous $f:\mathbf R\to\mathbf C$ and a real $B\geq0$ such that $|f(x)|\leq B$ on $[a,b]$,
$$\left|\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\right|\leq B(b-a).$$
